final_excerpt:
Posts now get the date it was in the author's own time zone when they published, and everyone sees that same date. All 10 tests pass: the 4 that were there before and 6 I added. Four of the new tests fail on the old code, which shows they catch the bugs.

**Changes in `journal.py`:**
- **`publish`** now takes the post's date from the author's own time zone (`client_tz`) instead of UTC. Before, someone in Tokyo posting on the morning of Mar 10 got Mar 9, and someone in Los Angeles posting on the evening of Mar 9 got Mar 10.
- **`display_date`** now returns the stored date unchanged for every vi
